# Custom build

A docs site the team built themselves: a Next.js, Gatsby, Astro, Remix or SvelteKit app, hand-written HTML, an in-house CMS, or a generator with no guide of its own. There is no platform config to map, so the code and the rendered site are the only sources of structure.

## Detect

- No other source guide matches. A framework dependency alone is not enough: `next` can be Nextra or Fumadocs, `astro` can be Starlight, `nuxt` can be Docus or Nuxt Content. Check those guides' Detect sections first.
- `.dita`/`.ditamap` files or a DITA-OT build mean DITA (`mint migrate --from dita`).
- Content lives in `.md`/`.mdx` files, JSON or YAML data, a headless CMS, pages written as components, or plain `.html` files.

## Get the source

### From the repo

- Content: a `content/`, `docs/` or `pages/` folder, data files, CMS fetch calls, or prose inside JSX or HTML. Convert the text of component pages, not their code.
- Navigation: read the component that renders the sidebar to find what feeds it: a config file (`sidebar.ts`, `nav.json`), a route manifest, front matter such as `order`, or links hard-coded in the JSX. That is the navigation data.
- URLs: route folders (`app/`, `pages/`, `src/pages/`) and, in `next.config.*`, `vercel.json`, `netlify.toml` or `_redirects`, the `basePath`, `trailingSlash` and `redirects` settings.

### From an export

A CMS export (JSON, CSV or Markdown) holds the content but rarely navigation or URLs. Take those from the repo or the live site.

### From the live site

Most custom sites have no raw Markdown endpoint: mirror rendered HTML and keep only the main content element. Check for a cleaner payload first: `__NEXT_DATA__` on Next.js Pages Router sites, `/page-data/<path>/page-data.json` on Gatsby.

## Config → docs.json

There is no config file. Find each Chrome item from `mint migrate --topic navigation` in the root layout, header and footer components, the `<head>` metadata, and the CSS variables or Tailwind theme.

## Navigation

Mirror the navigation data found in the repo. With only the live site, follow `mint migrate --topic navigation`, Reconstructed navigation.

## Content conversion

Read each custom component's source and map it by what it renders, not by its name (`mint migrate --topic conversion`, Components). Self-contained components carry over as component snippets; ones bound to the framework or that fetch data at runtime go in the report.

## Assets

Copy only files the content references, usually from `public/`, `static/` or `assets/`, at the same paths. Skip app code, styles, fonts and build output. Report CSS that hides or injects content.

## URLs and redirects

Take the old URL list from the build output or the live sitemap, not the route files: dynamic routes only become URLs at build time. Port existing redirects and any `basePath` prefix per `mint migrate --topic navigation`, Redirects.

## Known gaps

- Custom components with no Mintlify equivalent, and their interactivity.
- Search, auth, personalization or gated sections built into the app.
- Content fetched at runtime that the export or mirror did not capture.
